title: The plus construction is a presheaf, and its elements and equalities are described by refinements
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal F$ a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, and $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, morphisms of coverings, $\mathcal F^+(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal J_U^{opp}}H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, the classes $[\mathcal U,s]$, the maps $\mathcal F^+(h)$ and $\theta$ as in [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction]. Then: (1) every element of $\mathcal F^+(U)$ is of the form $[\mathcal U,s]$ for some covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$ and some $s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$; (2) for coverings $\mathcal U,\mathcal U'$ of $U$ and $s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, $s'\in H^0(\mathcal U',\mathcal F)$ one has $[\mathcal U,s]=[\mathcal U',s']$ if and only if there are a covering $\mathcal V$ of $U$ and morphisms of coverings $f:\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$, $f':\mathcal V\to\mathcal U'$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ with $f^*s=f'^*s'$ in $H^0(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)$; in particular, for $a,b\in\mathcal F(U)$, $\theta_U(a)=\theta_U(b)$ if and only if there is a covering $\{V_k\to U\}$ with $a|_{V_k}=b|_{V_k}$ for all $k$; (3) for every morphism $h:V\to U$, every covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$, every covering $\mathcal W$ of $V$ and every morphism of coverings $g:\mathcal W\to\mathcal U$ lying over $h$, one has $\mathcal F^+(h)([\mathcal U,s])=[\mathcal W,g^*s]$ for all $s\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$; in particular the maps $\mathcal F^+(h)$ do not depend on the chosen fibre products, and if $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $h$ factors as $V\xrightarrow{c}U_i\to U$ for some $i$, then $\mathcal F^+(h)([\mathcal U,s])=\theta_V(s_i|_V)$ with $s_i|_V=\mathcal F(c)(s_i)$; (4) with these maps $\mathcal F^+$ is a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$ ($\mathcal F^+(\mathrm{id}_U)=\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathcal F^+(h\circ k)=\mathcal F^+(k)\circ\mathcal F^+(h)$) and $\theta:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^+$ is a morphism of presheaves.

proof.text: Use the recorded sieve-based realization F⁺ = J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P. Every covering sieve contains a covering presieve, by Mathlib Precoverage.mem_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderComposition. Express that presieve as a ZeroHypercover and reindex its indexing type using ULift to Type (max u w). Thus every covering sieve S admits a family E whose generated sieve is contained in S. Apply Plus.exists_rep and refine its matching family to the generated sieve of E; Plus.eq_mk_iff_exists shows that the represented class is unchanged. This proves representative existence on actual covering families.

source.place: Section 00W1, paragraph after Remark 00W8 (representatives); generated-topology realization recorded in def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction; the family-to-sieve bridge is proved in Lean using the Mathlib characterization of generated covering sieves

proof.text: For equal classes, Plus.eq_mk_iff_exists gives a common covering sieve S on which the matching families agree. Choose a covering family W inside S as in Step 1. For every generator W.f i, membership in the generated sieves of E and F supplies factorizations through members of E and F; choosing these gives morphisms W → E and W → F. The matching-family compatibility condition identifies the pulled-back components with their values on W.f i, so they agree. Conversely, the two family morphisms give inclusions of the generated sieve of W into those of E and F. Every arrow in the former factors through some W.f i. Compatibility and the assumed equality on generators therefore identify the two refined matching families on every arrow. Plus.eq_mk_iff_exists then identifies the two classes. These arguments work also for an empty covering family.

source.place: Section 00W1, paragraph after Remark 00W8 (equality after common refinement); Mathlib ConcreteSheafification, Plus.eq_mk_iff_exists and Meq.condition

proof.text: For the equality criterion under θ, use Plus.toPlus_eq_mk to represent both images by Meq.mk on the maximal sieve, and use Plus.eq_mk_iff_exists. A covering family inside its witnessing sieve gives componentwise equality of the restrictions of the original two sections. Conversely, componentwise equality on a covering family extends to the generated sieve by matching-family compatibility; Plus.toPlus_mk on that generated sieve identifies the two images under θ.

source.place: Section 00W1, paragraph after Remark 00W8, specializing to the trivial covering; Mathlib Plus.toPlus_eq_mk and Plus.toPlus_mk

proof.text: A covering morphism g from W to E over h satisfies g.h₀ i ≫ E.f (g.s₀ i) = W.f i ≫ h. Downward closure therefore gives an inclusion of the generated sieve of W into the pullback of the generated sieve of E along h. Plus.res_mk_eq_mk_pullback computes restriction of the original class. Refine that pulled-back matching family to W; compatibility and the assumed component equations identify it with y on every generator, hence on the whole generated sieve. Plus.eq_mk_iff_exists proves the required equality of classes.

proof.text: Plus.toPlus_apply identifies restriction along each generator E.f i with θ applied to its component of x. Apply the plus presheaf map along c and use the naturality of toPlus to obtain the factorization formula. The presheaf laws and naturality in the original node are already bundled in plusObj and toPlus; independence of pullback choices follows from the covering-morphism formula of Step 4.

split_report.summary: Proof written in six steps from Stacks Sites Section 00W1, read against def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction (chosen fibre products, F^+(U) the chosen colimit over J_U^opp, F^+(h) via p_U). Stacks says the diagram H^0(-,F) on J_U^opp is filtered in the sense of Categories 002V (condition (3) only up to the diagram), not that J_U^opp is a filtered category, so Step 1 passes to the refinement preorder P_U (Lemma 00W7, new node lem-weil-pbc-site-covering-morphisms-same-h0-map) with the same cocones, and uses the existing common refinement node (00W6) for filteredness; (1),(2) then follow from the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise; the theta case of (2) is the unique morphism of a covering to {id_U}. (3) is proved directly from the cocone property: any morphism of coverings g over h factors as p_U o k with k in J_V (no use of 00W7); independence of fibre products and the factorization case (00W9) follow. (4) from (1) and (3) (identity, composite of the p's lies over h o k, theta via the factorization case). Statement and stmt_deps kept; the Mathlib verdict (sieve-based plusObj, not a one-line specialization) confirmed and a grep of Plus.lean added.

lean.statement: theorem plus_construction_presheaf {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition] [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u w)) : (∀ {U : C} (a : (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P).obj (op U)), ∃ (E : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (x : Meq P ⟨E.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck E.mem₀⟩), a = Plus.mk x) ∧ (∀ {U : C} (E F : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (x : Meq P ⟨E.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck E.mem₀⟩) (y : Meq P ⟨F.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck F.mem₀⟩), Plus.mk x = Plus.mk y ↔ ∃ (W : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (f : W ⟶ E) (g : W ⟶ F), ∀ i : W.I₀, P.map (f.h₀ i).op (x ⟨E.X (f.s₀ i), E.f (f.s₀ i), E.sieve₀_f _⟩) = P.map (g.h₀ i).op (y ⟨F.X (g.s₀ i), F.f (g.s₀ i), F.sieve₀_f _⟩)) ∧ (∀ {U : C} (a b : P.obj (op U)), (J.toGrothendieck.toPlus P).app (op U) a = (J.toGrothendieck.toPlus P).app (op U) b ↔ ∃ (E : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U), ∀ i : E.I₀, P.map (E.f i).op a = P.map (E.f i).op b) ∧ (∀ {V U : C} (h : V ⟶ U) (E : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (W : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J V) (g : (W.toPreZeroHypercover.pushforward h).Hom E.toPreZeroHypercover) (x : Meq P ⟨E.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck E.mem₀⟩) (y : Meq P ⟨W.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck W.mem₀⟩), (∀ i : W.I₀, y ⟨W.X i, W.f i, W.sieve₀_f i⟩ = P.map (g.h₀ i).op (x ⟨E.X (g.s₀ i), E.f (g.s₀ i), E.sieve₀_f _⟩)) → (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P).map h.op (Plus.mk x) = Plus.mk y) ∧ (∀ {V U : C} (E : Precoverage.ZeroHypercover.{max u w} J U) (x : Meq P ⟨E.sieve₀, J.generate_mem_toGrothendieck E.mem₀⟩) (i : E.I₀) (c : V ⟶ E.X i), (J.toGrothendieck.plusObj P).map (c ≫ E.f i).op (Plus.mk x) = (J.toGrothendieck.toPlus P).app (op V) (P.map c.op (x ⟨E.X i, E.f i, E.sieve₀_f i⟩)))
lean.note: Uses the dependency records: a small Precoverage site, Type-valued presheaf, ZeroHypercover covering families, and plusObj/toPlus for the generated topology. Meq on the sieve generated by a family is its canonical compatible-family extension; equality and restriction are stated componentwise on covering families. Functor and natural-transformation laws are already fields of plusObj and toPlus.
